targets.name: MACS0451-arc (MACS J0451+0006)
targets.cite: Jones+2010 MNRAS 404,1247 (z=2.014, mu=49+/-11, D=5+/-1 kpc, Vsin i=38+/-10, sig=80+/-5); Dessauges-Zavadsky+2015 A&A 577,A50 (CO(3-2), alpha_CO=4.36, M_mol=5.1e9, f_gas=0.71, mu=21.5); Schaerer+2015 A&A 576,L2 (ALMA [CII] 10sig, mu=49+/-5, M*~2.5e9)
targets.note: THE ONLY z~2 object in the literature with BOTH resolved kinematics AND a cold-gas mass. mu disagreement 21.5 vs 49 between two refereed papers = a factor 2.3 directly on any a0 readout. Vsin i/sig = 0.48 -> DISPERSION-DOMINATED, not a usable rotator as observed.

targets.name: OLAS A370-03097
targets.cite: Hirtenstein+2019 ApJ 880,54 Table 1 (dv=134 km/s, sig_int=68.8, v/sig=2.09)
targets.note: rotation-dominated; no gas mass, no published size

targets.name: OLAS M0717-02064
targets.cite: Hirtenstein+2019 ApJ 880,54 Table 1 (dv=142 km/s, sig_int=74.4, v/sig=1.64)
targets.note: *** LOWEST-M* rotation-dominated LENSED object known at z>2 (log M*=8.08, mu=6.48) -> the single best deep-MOND CANDIDATE in the published literature. But sig=74.4 km/s > V=71 km/s: pressure support is the whole problem.

targets.name: OLAS M0744-01203
targets.note: rotation-dominated but very turbulent

targets.name: OLAS M1149-00683
targets.note: 2nd-lowest-M* rotation-dominated lensed object at z>1.5; strong candidate

targets.name: OLAS M1149-01802
targets.note: best v/sig at z>2 in OLAS but log M*=9.70 -> too much mass for the cut

targets.name: OLAS M2129-00478
targets.note: LOWEST sigma at z>1.5 (37.4) but v/sig=0.47 -> NOT rotating. The anti-correlation in one object: the coldest low-mass z~2 lensed systems are the ones that are not rotators.

targets.name: OLAS M2129-01665
targets.note: essentially zero shear -> unusable as a rotator

targets.name: OLAS M2129-01833
targets.note: massive + hottest sigma in the sample

targets.name: Cl 0024+1709 arc
targets.note: *** THE BIG-RADIUS ROUTE: kinematics to R=10 kpc, the largest R in any lensed z>1.5 sample. R_req for a 2e10 M_bar is ~10 kpc -> this object sits AT the cut boundary by radius alone. But mu=1.38 (barely lensed) and sig>V.

targets.name: MACS J0744+3927 arc
targets.note: compact (R=1 kpc) + massive -> g_bar VERY far above the cut

targets.name: Cl 0949+5153 arc (merger)
targets.kin: Keck/OSIRIS AO Ha (RESOLVED, MERGER - two components)
targets.cite: Jones+2010 MNRAS 404,1247 Table 2 (D=7+/-1 kpc merging, sig_NE=71+/-2, sig_SW=57+/-2, M_dyn 13e9 / 7e9)
targets.note: MERGER -> disqualified for a rotation-based a0 readout

targets.name: A68-C0
targets.kin: CO unresolved; no resolved RC published
targets.note: gas mass IN HAND; needs the kinematics

targets.name: A68-h7
targets.note: too massive for the cut at any plausible radius

targets.name: A68-HLS115
targets.note: *** LOWEST M* with a REAL CO gas mass at z>1.5 (7.2e8). Best TIER-3 candidate: gas mass PUB, only the kinematics missing.

targets.name: A2218-Mult
targets.cite: Dessauges-Zavadsky+2015 A&A 577,A50 Table 1 (CO non-detection, M_mol<1.9e9, f_gas<0.51)
targets.note: mu=33.8 is the largest magnification of any gas-constrained z~1.5-2.5 target

targets.name: SL2S 0217 (SL2S J021737-051329)
targets.kin: NO resolved kinematics (sub-kpc Lya imaging only)
targets.cite: Berg+2018 ApJ 859,164 (M*<1e9, Z~1/20 Zsun, mu~17, 25-arcsec arc); Vanzella-class EELG; ALMA [CII] 3-4sigma TENTATIVE + CO(2-1) NON-detection, M_gas ~ few e8 (arXiv:2101.00841 = ApJ 2021); Lya imaging ApJ 2019 (10.3847/1538-4357/ab3daf)
targets.note: *** THE LOWEST-MASS LENSED z~2 GALAXY WITH ANY GAS CONSTRAINT AT ALL. But: [CII] is 30x FAINTER than the local dwarf [CII]-SFR relation at Z~0.05 Zsun, so the [CII]->M_gas conversion is BROKEN here. Gas mass is NOT reliable.

targets.name: A1689B11
targets.kin: Gemini/NIFS AO Ha (RESOLVED, COOL THIN disc)
targets.note: *** THE DECISIVE COUNTERWEIGHT ON PRESSURE SUPPORT, and it is in WARM IONIZED GAS (Ha, AO): sigma_outer = 15+/-2 km/s and V/sigma ~ 9-13 at z=2.54. So a 50-100 km/s dispersion is NOT an inevitable property of z~2 kinematics -- it is partly beam-smearing + seeing + tracer. But log M*=9.8 with r_1/2=2.6 kpc puts it far ABOVE the cut: this object is cold BECAUSE it is dense. R_out taken as 3 r_s = 3.9 kpc (the RC turnover is at 1.7 kpc).

targets.name: DSFG850.95
targets.cite: Drew+2018 ApJ 869,58 (arXiv:1811.01958): V_flat=285+/-12, sig=48+/-4, flat between 6-14 kpc, f_DM=0.44+/-0.08 at the H-band half-light radius
targets.note: UNLENSED. The BIG-RADIUS route in its purest form: R_out=14 kpc is the largest at z~1.5-2.5 anywhere. Massive, so still above the cut -- but it shows the radius lever is real without lensing.

targets.name: zC-400569 (cold-tracer control)
targets.cite: Lelli+2023 A&A 672,A106 (aa45105-22): sigma_CO <~15 km/s, V/sigma >~17-22, systematically BELOW ionized-gas IFU dispersions
targets.note: *** THE PRESSURE-SUPPORT EXISTENCE PROOF: cold tracers at cosmic noon give sigma <~15 km/s, not the 50-100 km/s of warm ionized gas. Massive and unlensed, so useless for the cut -- but it is the decisive methodological benchmark.

targets.name: Big Wheel (reference, in compilation)
targets.cite: Nature Astronomy s41550-025-02500-2 (arXiv:2409.17956): r_1/2=9.6 kpc, M*=3.7e11, rotation consistent with the LOCAL Tully-Fisher relation
targets.note: already carried in the committed compilation as a0_eff/a0(0)~1.0-1.3 +/-0.22 dex; listed here only to show the big-radius route at z>3

pools.name: KLASS (KMOS Lens-Amplified Spectroscopic Survey)
pools.cite: Girard+2020 MNRAS 497,173 (arXiv:2006.14633); first results Mason+2017 ApJ 838,14
pools.status: 44/52 resolved kinematics; median v_rot/sigma0 ~ 2.5; NO gas masses; KMOS SEEING-LIMITED (~0.6-0.7 arcsec ~ 5-6 kpc at z=2) -> outer radii and beam smearing are the limitation, not sample size
pools.verdict: LARGEST existing lensed low-mass cosmic-noon kinematic pool; the z>1.5 low-mass tail is the natural parent catalogue for a JWST follow-up

pools.name: OLAS (OSIRIS Lens-Amplified Survey)
pools.status: AO-assisted (good resolution); 8 objects at z=1.5-2.3 tabulated above; ~9/16 rotation-dominated; NO gas masses; NO published source-plane radii
pools.verdict: the ONLY AO-resolution lensed sample that reaches log M* ~ 8 at z~2

pools.name: MUSE Lensing Cluster Survey / MUSE-DARK II
pools.cite: Jeanneau+2026 A&A (arXiv:2603.28856), lensing-aware GalPaK3D forward modelling
pools.status: EXACTLY the right object class (lensed, low-mass, 3D lensing-aware modelling) but the REDSHIFT CEILING IS HARD: MUSE's 4750-9350 A window puts [OII]3727 out of range beyond z~1.5, so this sample CANNOT be pushed to z~2
pools.verdict: the method to copy; the wrong instrument for z~2 -> JWST/NIRSpec required

pools.name: SGAS lensed arcs with ALMA cold gas
pools.cite: Solimano+2024 A&A (aa51892-24) 'Molecular gas budget of strongly magnified low-mass star-forming galaxies at cosmic noon'; + Solimano+2021
pools.status: only 3/12 CO DETECTIONS (J0033 z=1.917, J0108 z=2.514, J1050A z=3.625); the rest are UPPER LIMITS; no resolved kinematics reported
pools.verdict: *** THE HARD NUMBER ON GAS MASSES: a dedicated ALMA program on magnified low-mass cosmic-noon arcs detects CO in 25% of targets. This is why g_bar is not computable a priori.

pools.name: LEGGOS (JWST lensed clumps survey)
pools.cite: LEGGOS II, arXiv:2606.20804 (SGAS J111020.0+645950.8 at z=2.481, JWST NIRCam + NIRSpec + archival HST, ~30x total magnification); source reconstruction Johnson+2017 ApJ 843,78 and ApJL 843,L21
pools.status: JWST-era lensed z~2.5 target with a modern lens model and NIRSpec data; whether the NIRSpec mode delivers a SOURCE-PLANE ROTATION CURVE (IFU) vs clump spectroscopy (MSA) is a CANDIDATE-TO-CHECK, not asserted here
pools.verdict: highest-priority archival check (hands off to D-2)

pools.name: TEMPLATES (JWST ERS 1355)
pools.cite: JWST ERS program 1355 (stsci.edu/jwst/phase2-public/1355.pdf): NIRSpec + MIRI IFU of 4 lensed galaxies at 1<z<4 -- SGAS J1723+3411 (z=1.33), SGAS J1226+2152 (z=2.92), SPT0418-47 (z=4.22), SPT2147-50 (z=3.76)
pools.status: REAL NIRSpec IFU data on lensed arcs exists, but the two z-bracketing targets are z=1.33 and z=2.92 -- NEITHER lands in 1.5-2.5 -- and all four are luminous/massive, not deep-MOND candidates
pools.verdict: proves the OBSERVING MODE works on lensed arcs; provides no cut-passing target
